title: Steering-Induced Incoherence x Monitor Blindness: Do Degraded Outputs Slip Past Safety Classifiers?

original_idea.body: Steering-Induced Incoherence x Monitor Blindness: degraded harmful outputs under heavy steering may evade safety classifiers trained on coherent text.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Concrete scenario: harmful actors exploit a monitoring blind spot; chain from finding to monitoring-robustness is explicit and defensible.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Clear inherited methodology (steering sweep + open guard model scoring); novice + mentor can execute.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped single experiment: sweep steering strength, score with classifier, compare to ground-truth labels.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent-friendly: public models/guards, no internal access, monitoring-robustness is lab-deprioritized.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference-only on a small model plus a guard model; single mid GPU at most.

novelty.reasoning: Classifiers failing on OOD/incoherent inputs is partly studied but the steering-induced angle may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Robustness of safety classifiers to degraded text exists but the steering-coherence interaction angle may be open.
